errors.too_many_attempts: Too many failed attempts. Try again in {{minutes}} minutes.
errors.setup_token: The setup link is wrong. Open the one printed in the panel's log.
errors.setup_done: This panel is already set up.
errors.weak_password: A password needs at least 8 characters.
errors.invalid_username: That username isn't valid: letters, digits and the allowed symbols only, of a fitting length.
errors.internal: Server error. Check the panel's log.
errors.port_conflict: This port is already in use.
errors.invalid_certificate: The certificate is not valid or the key does not match.
errors.certificate_in_use: An inbound still uses this certificate.
errors.invalid_address: An address or domain is needed.
errors.invalid_target: A target is a domain name.
errors.invalid_on_hold: An on-hold user needs a number of days.
errors.invalid_name: A name of 1 to 64 characters is needed.
errors.too_many: That's more than allowed at once.
errors.not_found: Not found; it may have been deleted.
errors.invalid_subscription: The subscription settings are not valid: {{message}}
errors.invalid_core: The core does not accept these settings: {{message}}
errors.invalid_preset: The preset could not be made: {{message}}
errors.warp_failed: The WARP account could not be made: {{message}}
errors.invalid_log_level: That is not a log level.
errors.session_required: This can only be done signed in to the panel, not with an API key.
errors.account_disabled: This account is disabled. Ask a sudo admin to turn it on.
errors.role_required: An admin who is not sudo needs a role.
errors.role_in_use: Admins have this role; change theirs first.
errors.cannot_change_self: You cannot change your own role or status, or delete yourself; ask another sudo admin.
errors.last_sudo: This is the last sudo admin; make another first.
errors.invalid_heir: The users need another admin to go to.
errors.invalid_permission: One of the permissions is not valid.
errors.user_limit_reached: You have reached the most users you may own.
errors.quota_exceeded: Your data quota is not enough for this change.
errors.quota_unlimited: The user needs a data limit: your quota counts it.
errors.group_not_allowed: You may not give one of these groups.
errors.invalid_api_key: The API key is not valid.
errors.ip_not_allowed: This key may not be used from this address.
errors.permission_exceeds: A key cannot have more than you may do yourself.
errors.too_many_keys: You have the most keys allowed; revoke one first.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Users' subscriptions and your account's security
settings.passwordBody: Changing it signs out every other session of yours.
settings.totpBody: Besides the password, signing in will need a code from your authenticator app.
settings.totpScan: Scan this QR code with an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Aegis, …), then enter the 6-digit code.
settings.totpSecret: Or type this key in by hand:
settings.totpDisableBody: Enter your password and a current code to turn it off.

inbounds.title: Inbounds
inbounds.subtitle: Where the core accepts its users
inbounds.noCertificate: Add a certificate on the Certificates page first
inbounds.targetHint: The site connections look like; it needs TLS 1.3 and HTTP/2
inbounds.sniffingHint: Reads the real domain from HTTP, TLS and QUIC for better routing
inbounds.deleteBody: “{{name}}” and its hosts are deleted and its connections end.
inbounds.empty: No inbound yet. The core starts with the first one.

certificates.title: Certificates
certificates.subtitle: TLS certificates for inbounds
certificates.name: Name
certificates.empty: No certificate yet. Automatic Let's Encrypt arrives in phase 10; for now, upload one.

hosts.title: Hosts
hosts.subtitle: Addresses users reach each inbound by (for links and subscriptions)
hosts.portHint: Empty means the inbound's own port
hosts.allowInsecureHint: For testing only; it removes the connection's security
hosts.empty: No host yet. Without one, links use the server's address.

users.title: Users
users.subtitle: Each user reaches inbounds through its groups, and the panel holds it to its limits.
users.namesLike: {{first}} to {{last}}; names already taken are skipped.
users.onHoldHint: Its time starts on its first connection.
users.onHoldDaysHint: Its first connection sets the expiry this far ahead.
users.onHoldTimeoutHint: If it never connects by then, its time starts on its own.
users.groupsHint: The user reaches the inbounds its groups give.
users.ipLimitHint: Addresses that came last are cut off.
users.holdFor_one: {{count, number}} day after its first connection
users.holdFor_other: {{count, number}} days after its first connection
users.revokeBody: {{name}} gets a new UUID, password and subscription link, and its open sessions end. Its old config stops working.
users.deleteBody: {{name}} is deleted for good and its sessions end.
users.empty: No users yet. Create the first one.
users.nextPlanHint: When the user runs out of data or time, it moves on to this plan instead of being cut off (once).
users.carryOverHint: Data left of the old limit is added to the new one.
users.setGroupsHint: The selected users end up in exactly these groups.
users.bulkResetBody_one: This period's usage of {{count, number}} user goes back to zero.
users.bulkResetBody_other: This period's usage of {{count, number}} users goes back to zero.
users.bulkRevokeBody_one: {{count, number}} user gets new credentials; its old config stops working.
users.bulkRevokeBody_other: {{count, number}} users get new credentials; their old configs stop working.
users.bulkDeleteBody_one: {{count, number}} user is deleted for good.
users.bulkDeleteBody_other: {{count, number}} users are deleted for good.
users.hwidLimitHint: Devices the subscription may be fetched on (from the app's x-hwid header). Blank means any.

groups.title: Groups
groups.subtitle: A group gives access to some inbounds; its users get all of them.
groups.name: Name
groups.allInboundsHint: Inbounds made later are included too.
groups.deleteBody_one: {{name}} is deleted, and its {{count, number}} user loses the access it gave.
groups.deleteBody_other: {{name}} is deleted, and its {{count, number}} users lose the access it gave them.

templates.title: Templates
templates.subtitle: Ready-made limits for making users quickly.
templates.name: Name
templates.onHoldHint: Users are made on hold, and their days count from their first connection.
templates.groupsHint: Blank keeps the groups picked in the user form.
templates.deleteBody: {{name}} is deleted; users made with it stay as they are.

subscription.title: Subscription of {{name}}
subscription.urlHint: Put this link in the user's app; its configs and usage stay up to date on their own.
subscription.noConfigs: No configs: the user is not active, or its groups give no inbound.
subscription.neverFetched: The subscription has not been fetched yet.
subscription.settingsBody: Users' subscription links, and what apps show from them.
subscription.publicUrlHint: The address links are made with; blank for the one the panel is opened at.
subscription.serverAddressHint: For inbounds without a host; blank for the name the app fetched the subscription by.
subscription.hwidRequired: Only apps that send a device id
subscription.hwidRequiredHint: For a user with a device limit, an app that sends no x-hwid is refused.
subscription.templateHint: Your own HTML for browsers; {{data}} becomes the subscription as JSON. Blank for the built-in page.

logs.title: Logs
logs.subtitle: What the panel and the core are doing, live.
logs.empty: No line yet with this filter. The panel's log level is set with ZUI_LOG.
logs.levelOfProcess: Log level of the panel and the core

core.title: Core settings
core.subtitle: Outbounds, routing, DNS and zray's own features; every change is checked first and stored only if the core accepts it.
core.proposedBar: The preset is loaded in the editor; review it and apply.
core.nothingToApply: Everything is as the core has it now.
core.applied_restarted: Applied; the ports changed over without a gap.
core.applied_stopped: Saved; no inbound is on, so the core is stopped.
core.tagHint: The name rules refer to it by.
core.outboundsBody: The ways users' traffic reaches the internet. The first outbound takes whatever no rule sends elsewhere.
core.linkHint: A vless, vmess, trojan, ss, hysteria2 or tuic link, or warp://. Copy it from another app or server.
core.warpHint: The WARP account's keys are made on this server and only their public halves go to Cloudflare. The server must be able to reach Cloudflare's API.
core.dialThroughHint: The connection to this outbound's server goes out through another outbound, such as WARP: a proxy chain.
core.fragmentHint: Hides the site name from the filter; only for TLS and Reality outbounds.
core.allowInsecureHint: For tests only; it leaves the connection open to interception.
core.domainStrategyHint: AsIs hands the name to the destination as it is; UseIP resolves it first.
core.blackholeHint: Whatever reaches this outbound is dropped without a word; for blocking destinations by rule.
core.torHint: Traffic goes through Tor. The core must be built with Tor support.
core.jsonOutboundHint: Write any Xray or zray outbound as it is.
core.deleteOutboundBody: {{tag}} is removed from the editor; Apply sends it to the core.
core.deleteOutboundUsed: {{tag}} is still named by {{uses}}. If you delete it, the core's check will refuse until you fix those.
core.deleteLastOutbound: This is the only outbound. The core refuses settings without one.
core.routingBody: Rules are tried in order, and the first that matches sends the traffic.
core.routingStrategy_IPIfNonMatch: IPIfNonMatch (the IP if no rule matched the name)
core.routingStrategy_IPOnDemand: IPOnDemand (whenever an IP rule needs it)
core.routingStrategyHint: For geoip rules on traffic that arrives with a name, pick one of the IP modes.
core.blockPrivateHint: Users cannot reach the server's loopback, internal network and link-local addresses, so they cannot get at services that trust the server itself. This rule always runs first.
core.rulesBody: A rule has some conditions that must all hold; within a list, one entry is enough.
core.noRules: No rules: all traffic goes to the default outbound.
core.ruleHint: A blank condition means anything. Give at least one condition unless this is the last, catch-all rule.
core.ruleMatchesAll: With no condition this rule takes all the traffic, and the rules after it never run.
core.ruleDomainHint: One per line: domain:, full:, keyword:, regexp: or geosite:.
core.ruleIpHint: An address, a CIDR range or geoip:, one per line.
core.ruleUsersHint: Usernames; the rule only applies to these users.
core.deleteRuleBody: Rule number {{number, number}} is removed from the editor.
core.balancersBody: Makes several outbounds one: traffic is spread among them or goes to the best. A rule can point at a balancer.
core.balancerSelectorHint: One tag or tag prefix per line; every outbound starting with it is chosen.
core.strategyNeedsObservatory: It needs the observatory to measure the outbounds.
core.deleteBalancerBody: Balancer {{tag}} is removed from the editor.
core.observatoryBody: Every so often fetches an address through each outbound, so the least-ping and least-load balancers know which is better.
core.observatorySubjectsHint: One tag or tag prefix per line.
core.geodataBody: Rules like geosite:category-ir and geoip:ir need these lists; a tag that is not in them matches nothing.
core.geodataManage: Keep the lists up to date
core.geodataManageHint: The core downloads them from several mirrors and refreshes them daily.
core.geodataTags: {{sites, number}} geosite tags and {{ips, number}} geoip tags loaded
core.geodataApplyFirst: Once the settings are applied, the download status shows here.
core.dnsBody: How the names users ask for are found.
core.queryStrategyHint: If the server has no IPv6, IPv4 only saves pointless attempts.
core.leakPolicyHint: On a server that sends traffic out directly, its own resolver is the right one. With any proxy outbound the core forbids it itself, since it would answer outside the tunnel.
core.dnsDisableCacheHint: Every query is asked afresh; slower.
core.dnsServersBody: Asked in order. A resolver with a list of domains only answers for those.
core.noDnsServers: No resolvers; without one no name is found.
core.dnsAddressHint: An IP, or https://… (DoH), tls://… (DoT), quic://… (DoQ), or localhost for the server's own resolver.
core.dnsExpect: The answer must be in these IPs
core.dnsExpectHint: An answer outside them is dropped and the next resolver is asked.
core.dnsTagHint: To name this resolver from a rule (directVia).
core.dnsSkipFallback: Leave out of the fallback chain
core.dnsSkipFallbackHint: If it gives no answer, the next resolver is not tried.
core.deleteDnsServerBody: This resolver is removed from the editor.
core.dnsHostsBody: A name that gets a fixed answer without asking anyone.
core.dnsHostsLabel: One per line: a name and its answer
core.dnsHostsHint: Separate several IPs with commas; an answer of #block blocks the name.
core.presetCardBody: A ready-made set for the Iranian network: three DNS tiers (anti-sanction, domestic, encrypted), routing of Iranian domains and IPs, ad blocking and the geodata lists. It replaces the panel's current outbounds and rules.
core.presetBody: The proposed settings are loaded in the editor and not yet on the core; you can look, edit, and then apply.
core.presetLinksHint: One link per line. The first takes whatever no rule sends elsewhere.
core.fragmentBody: For each TLS or Reality outbound, choose whether its first hello is split in pieces.
core.cleanIpBody: Among several Cloudflare edge addresses, finds the one that works on this network and points the CDN-fronted outbounds at it.
core.jsonBody: All the settings but the inbounds (which have their own page). The blockPrivate key is the panel's own; the rest is the core's JSON.
core.geodataNeeded: Your rules or DNS name geosite or geoip tags, but no lists are loaded; those tags match nothing.
core.dnsForcedStrict: An outbound sends traffic through another server; then the core never uses the server's own resolver, whatever the system-resolver setting says.
core.dnsNoResolver: You now have only the system resolver, so no name resolves, for direct connections either. Add a resolver by address (DoH, DoT or UDP) or use the Iran preset.

quick.certificateHint: Upload a certificate and key for TLS inbounds

forbidden.title: No access
forbidden.body: Your admin may not open this page. If you need it, ask a sudo admin to change your role.

access.title: Admins and access
access.subtitle: Admins, roles, and what each may see and change; resellers see only the users they made.
access.newPasswordHint: Leave empty to keep the current one. A new password signs the admin out everywhere.
access.sudoHint: A sudo admin sees everything and manages admins and roles. Give it only to people you trust.
access.roleHint: The role sets what they may do; the quotas and allowed groups below are for this admin alone.
access.dataQuotaHint: The total data they may hand out to their users. 0 means no cap; with a quota, users must have a data limit.
access.groupsHint: The groups they may give their users; none ticked means all.
access.enabledHint: A disabled admin cannot sign in and their API keys stop working; their users stay connected.
access.selfHint: You cannot turn yourself off or change your own role; ask another sudo admin.
access.unlimitedUsers_one: {{count, number}} user without a data limit
access.unlimitedUsers_other: {{count, number}} users without a data limit
access.deleteBody_one: They own {{count, number}} user, and their API keys are deleted too. The user is not deleted: it goes to the admin you pick.
access.deleteBody_other: They own {{count, number}} users, and their API keys are deleted too. The users are not deleted: they go to the admin you pick.
access.ownUsersHint: An admin with this role sees and changes only the users they made (a reseller).
access.permissionsHint: “View” only shows; “Manage” also allows changes. Managing admins and roles is for sudo admins alone.
access.deleteRoleUsed_one: {{count, number}} admin has the role “{{name}}”; change theirs first.
access.deleteRoleUsed_other: {{count, number}} admins have the role “{{name}}”; change theirs first.
access.quotaUnlimitedWarn: Some of your users have no data limit, which a quota cannot count.

sectionHint.users: List, make and edit users and their traffic
sectionHint.monitor: The server's CPU, memory, disk and network
sectionHint.logs: The live log and its level

audit.title: Activity log
audit.subtitle: Everything admins did, with time and address; failed sign-ins too. Entries are kept for {{days}} days.

user.devices_clear: Removed all of a user's devices

admin.reset_2fa: Turned off an admin's two-factor sign-in

developer.title: API
developer.subtitle: The panel can be run from scripts and bots too: everything the dashboard does.
developer.keysBody: An API key is like an admin's password for scripts: it works with the permissions you give it and from the addresses you name. The whole key is shown only once.
developer.noKeyAccess: Your admin may not make API keys.
developer.noKeys: You have not made a key yet.
developer.keyNameHint: To tell it apart, such as “Telegram bot”.
developer.scopeHint_read: Only to view every part you can view yourself; it changes nothing.
developer.scopeHint_custom: Set each part on its own; never more than you may do yourself.
developer.scopeHint_full: Anything you can do. For tools you trust.
developer.allowedIpsHint: One address or range per line (such as 10.0.0.0/8). Empty means from anywhere.
developer.revokeBody: The key “{{name}}” stops working at once, and this cannot be undone.
developer.keyMadeBody: Copy it now: the panel keeps only a hash of it and will not show it again.
developer.realCall: This call really runs and changes things.
developer.streamNote: This is a live stream; try it with cURL or EventSource.
